title: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.smoothPurityIso
statement: Let l be a prime and k a field of characteristic p>0 with p != l. Let X, Y be separated schemes of finite type over Spec k (objects of Over (Spec k)) and f:X\toY a morphism over k whose underlying morphism of schemes is smooth of pure relative dimension d. Write Qlb for the condensed ring Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj l, Qlb_Y for the tensor unit of the monoidal category D^b_c(Y)[[Qlb]] of bounded constructible module objects over Qlb on the pro-etale site of Y, Rf^! for boundedConstructibleUpperShriek (the right adjoint of Rf_!, built from a Nagata compactification of f), and Qlb_X(d) for the Tate twist tateTwistDerived X l d of WeilConjectures.TateTwist.ProEtale [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]. Then there is an isomorphism (Rf^! Qlb_Y) ~= Qlb_X(d)[2d] in D(Mod_{Qlb_X}) (after the fully faithful inclusion of D^b_c(X)[[Qlb]]). The upstream declaration is a chosen isomorphism (data, @[no_expose]). Its intended SGA normalization is obtained by reconstructing the inverse finite-coefficient smooth-purity comparisons, extending coefficients to the finite-extension-valued condensed Qlb ring, and identifying Lf^* of the unit with the unit. The common-stage Qlb category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] and the condensed-module category are related by coefficient realization, not identified by definition.

proof.text: Keep the original field k and the actual target coefficient category. Put B_T=p_T^*underline(Omega), Omega=Qbar_l, for T=X,Y; here underline(Omega) is the finite-extension-valued condensed ring Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ell, not the ring of all continuous Omega-valued functions. Use the archived full bounded constructible module-object categories C^c_Omega(T) described in [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. The coefficient unit B_Y in degree zero belongs to this category: on the single stratum Y it is the cokernel of the zero map from a rank-zero free module to a rank-one free module. It has Tor amplitude [0,0], since B_Y tensor^L_{B_Y} N=N for any module sheaf N. Fix the same Nagata compactification c=(j,g) as the target, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. In the notation of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction], G is the chosen boundedConstructibleUpperShriek, the composite of the chosen proper right adjoint and open restriction, with its composite adjunction. This is exactly the functor specified in that theorem, rather than a common-stage exceptional functor. All schemes in the compactification are separated finite type over k by the setting node. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only its zero and unit ideals; they have finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The same hypotheses apply to the finite-type geometric constructions below. The integer ell is invertible on these schemes because char(k) differs from ell. The target has d in N. No finite-field or algebraic-closure condition on k is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base] to the original field k and to the finite coefficient rings A_n=Z/ell^n Z. Its diagonal/DNC construction gives the constructible exceptional adjoint Rf_n^! and a normalized isomorphism gamma_n:A_{n,X}(d)[2d] ~= Rf_n^!A_{n,Y}. The statement includes the ordinary-etale origin, bounded constructibility and finite-Tor preservation needed for the coefficient unit, so no algebraic-closure or finite-field hypothesis is introduced.

proof.text: The same finite node supplies the counit-defined coefficient comparisons for A_r \to A_n, their quotient cocycle, and the equality c_{r,n} o (gamma_r tensor^L A_n)=gamma_n after the canonical twist reduction. Thus the diagonal, DNC and affine-space orientation maps are the specified normalized maps at every finite level; for d=0 they are the identity adjunction.

proof.text: Form the strict towers M_n=A_{n,X}(d)[2d] and L_n=A_{n,Y} with the root-power and quotient transitions. By [lem-pur-condensed-tate-integral-tower], these transitions are normalized and cocyclic, their finite levels have compatible etale-origin witnesses, and the derived limits M and L lie in the completed integral constructible categories with canonical reductions M_n and L_n. The finite maps gamma_n identify M_n with the corresponding exceptional tower and are concentrated in degree -2d on X.

source.place: Steps 1-3: strict normalized tower and uniform reconstruction

proof.text: Apply case (b) of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction] to the reconstructed towers: all M_n have the common degree -2d and the gamma_n commute with reductions by Steps 2-3. Its functorial good-truncation clause identifies the derived systems without choosing a lift from unrelated evaluated isomorphisms, and its conclusion gives c:U_X(M) ~= G(U_Y L), where G is the target's chosen boundedConstructibleUpperShriek with its counit.

source.place: Adic reconstruction and exceptional-adjoint comparison at the coefficient unit

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-condensed-tate-realization] with d=0 to the scheme Y and the reconstructed tower L=R\lim_n A_{n,Y} of Step 4, which lies in the completed integral constructible category of Y with canonical reductions A_{n,Y}. It gives the unit comparison e_Y:U_Y(L)\cong B_Y, the identity at d=0 after R_Y\cong\lim_n A_{n,Y}; this is the final clause of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction] that U_Y sends the integral coefficient object to the condensed tensor unit. B_Y in degree zero is the tensor unit of the target category (Step 1). Hence a=c^{-1}\circ G(e_Y^{-1}):G(B_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X(M), with inverse G(e_Y)\circ c, where c is the isomorphism of Step 5.

source.place: Unit comparison and composition with the reconstructed exceptional comparison

proof.text: By [lem-pur-condensed-tate-realization], the actual condensed coefficient realization of M has an ambient isomorphism b:iota_X(U_X(M)) ~= tateTwistDerived X ell d[2d]. This uses the finite-level ring quotient and roots-of-unity identifications, the root-power limit, and the balanced tensor comparison; it is the identity for d=0.

source.place: Step 2: transport of the adic Tate line through rational and Qbar coefficients

proof.text: The required ambient isomorphism is b\circ\iota_X(a), where a is the isomorphism of Step 6 and b that of Step 7. Its inverse is \iota_X(a^{-1})\circ b^{-1}; the inverse equations follow by associativity and functoriality of \iota_X. The source is the chosen upper-shriek image G(B_Y) of the condensed tensor unit and the target is the target's shifted Tate object tateTwistDerived X ell d[2d].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q33-c582798af (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against the exact source Defs.lean:76-92 and the master UpperShriek definitions (the verbatim exhibit at lines 214-264). The target keeps every hypothesis: arbitrary field k of characteristic p>0 with p≠ℓ, X and Y separated and of finite type, f smooth of pure relative dimension d. It also keeps the finite-extension-valued padicAlgClRingObj coefficient category, the tensor unit, the chosen Nagata boundedConstructibleUpperShriek (right adjoint of Rg_* followed by j^*) and tateTwistDerived. It is not weakened, and the route cites no SGA source. Steps 2-3: lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base holds over any field and gives γ_n and its counit-transpose reduction compatibility; this agrees with b_{A,B} of lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons, so the transitions match. Step 5: I checked every hypothesis of case (b) of lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction (single degree −2d, intertwined transitions, M∈I_X, L∈I_Y with their reductions). The new tower node is true: the twists are locally free of rank one and Rlim of surjective transitions is Z_ℓ(d)[2d]. It is not a duplicate, because thm-pur-adic-reconstruction is stated only for k = F̄_q (def-pur-conventions). The new realization node is true; I checked R_X/ℓ^n=(Z/ℓ^n)_X, the n=0 term, the balanced tensor and d=0. Edge cases d=0, empty schemes, n=1 and k=F_p(t) passed. I made four repairs in fixes/. (1) C4: Step 6 cited lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback for U_Y(L)≅B_Y, which that node does not state; it now cites the realization node at d=0 and the unit clause of the reconstruction node. (2) Typo: Step 8 named the wrong steps for a and b (they are Steps 6 and 7); it is now an elementary step with empty uses, and proof_deps is recomputed. (3) Hypothesis fault: lem-pur-condensed-tate-realization allowed an arbitrary scheme, but U_X (through J_X) exists only for separated finite-type schemes over a field of characteristic p>0, p≠ℓ, and needs M_d∈I_X. I restricted the scheme to that setting, wrote U_X explicitly and made membership of M_d a hypothesis that Step 4 supplies; the conclusion is unchanged. (4) B2/B3: lem-pur-condensed-tate-integral-tower used Rf_n^! and γ_n without introducing or citing them; it is now in TeX, cites its notions in the text, and has a larger stmt_deps.
